headline: Three classic terminals brought back from the dead
lede: Seedpin batch 16 restores what the Feb ports never had: a real end to a run. Pong, Asteroids and Centipede now score, die and restart like the machines did — and every filed seed replays the world.

notes.text: Asteroids finally obeys the 1979 law: rocks pay 20/50/100 (a full big-rock chain lands exactly 520), three lives with a grace respawn, waves refill — and the ship can now die, which in the old port it flatly could not.

Centipede's dead score code is alive: head 100 / body 10 / mushroom 1, cut segments spawn a new eyed head behind the gap, and a touch costs a life while the mushroom field persists — arcade death, not hard reset.

Pong ships an honest terminal: the 1972 machine had no forced cap, so q/Escape ends the match and the score stays on the table; starts now actually reset it (the old code literally wondered 'Reset score? Maybe').
Studio plumbing: the GitHub rescue shim had four real bugs (null field posts, malformed PR lookups, a check-runs crash) — all fixed, and the rule-5 merge path now runs verbatim again.

look.text: Asteroids with real lives, waves and 20/50/100 scoring
Centipede: head shots pay 100 and bodies split with a new head
